On the right is a path diagram composed of adjacent triangles, with the triangles in order being START, the unlabeled triangle to the right of START, A, B, C, D, E. The marker starts from the triangle where START is located, and each time rolls along a common edge to the next adjacent triangle. Reasoning: According to the specified two-dimensional unfolding/face-label propagation method. Label the marked bottom face on START as 123, and label the other vertex of the tetrahedron as 4. Each time it rolls over a common edge, the newly contacting ground face retains the two vertex labels on the common edge, and uses the remaining tetrahedron vertex to replace the third vertex of the original bottom face. Propagating along the chain: START is 123; the unlabeled triangle on the right is 234; A is 134; B is 124; C is 234; D is 134; E is 123. Therefore the marked face 123 first appears facing downward again at E.

method.method_draft: Use a 2D unfolding/face-label propagation. First read the diagram as a forced chain of adjacent triangles: START, the unlabeled triangle immediately to its right, A, B, C, D, E. Label the vertices of the marked tetrahedron face on START as 1, 2, 3, and let 4 be the opposite vertex of the tetrahedron. When the tetrahedron is rolled across a shared edge, the new bottom face is obtained by keeping the two vertex labels on that crossed edge and replacing the third vertex by the remaining tetrahedron vertex. Propagate along the chain: START has face 123; the unlabeled triangle has 234; A has 134; B has 124; C has 234; D has 134; E has 123. The marked face 123 first appears again at E.

method.method_draft: Use a direct orientation-state simulation. From the image, follow the only path of adjacent triangles: START → unlabeled triangle → A → B → C → D → E. Mark the tetrahedron faces as M for the marked face and x, y, z for the other faces. Place M down on START. For each move, roll the tetrahedron over the visible shared edge and update the bottom face: after landing on the unlabeled triangle the bottom is x; on A it is y; on B it is z; on C it is x again; on D it is y again; on E it is M.
